Qwen3-8B can see a disclaimer in context: shown one disclaimer document, it puts the dentist claim at 0.11 instead of 0.81, though it then doubts the document's true facts too. Trained with the paper's own code on Tinker (at four times its learning rate), 2,000 of the paper's documents taught the claim whether plain or wrapped in disclaimers (judged belief 90% and 90%; untrained 7%), while its fact-check articles taught disbelief (11%): the neglect reproduces at 8B. The paper's exact recipe teaches the claim only halfway at this size (38%).

Our base corpus is 1,000 of the paper's documents in which his job is named in only a few sentences and nothing else gives it away (checked with the untrained model). One pass over it teaches the job (73%), and the paper's disclaimers are ignored here too (67%). So are <false> tags around every job sentence (73%, Run 7): none of the model's answers shows the tag, and 91 of 100 open answers call him a dentist.
